app.title: Food Systems Financing Intelligence (FSFI)
app.subtitle: FSFI · Rwanda government dashboard
app.ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources
app.official_banner: An official platform of the Government of Rwanda

landing.components_lead: The index uses indicators that reflect how Rwanda's food system works, from hillside production and livestock to post-harvest handling, markets, nutrition, finance, research and the environment.
landing.hero_title_2: Build a more resilient food system.
landing.hero_p1: Food Systems Financing Intelligence helps the Government of Rwanda and its development partners decide how to allocate funds across the food system, set national targets and track results.
landing.hero_p2: In Rwanda, FSFI tracks 37 indicators grouped into 8 components. Better-targeted allocation across these areas strengthens resilience and reduces exposure to shocks.
landing.components_sub: Defined for Rwanda's context and aligned with national priorities.
landing.cta_access_body: Sign in with your government credentials.
landing.feature1_desc: See where financing pressure is highest across Rwanda's 37 indicators and 8 components, year by year. Every assessment is saved, so decisions can be traced and reviewed.
landing.feature2_desc: Follow agriculture budgets through the same indicator framework: multi-year totals, changes in the mix and volatility. Spending data sits alongside the stress index.
landing.feature3_desc: Test efficiency, reallocation and multi-year envelopes, including PSTA 5 views, before committing to scenarios, MTEF ceilings or partner agreements.
landing.feature4_desc: Track trends by fiscal year, priority area and, where data exist, by province and district. Reports and alerts support follow-up across government and partners.

about_page.hero_lead: Food Systems Financing Intelligence is a decision-support platform. It helps the Government of Rwanda see where to invest and what results to expect. Donors and partners use the same evidence to align their support with national food system goals.
about_page.challenge_intro: Food system budgets must cover many priorities. Decision makers need clear answers: where money does the most good, how spending relates to resilience, and how to explain trade-offs to partners and the public.
about_page.challenge_q1: Where should the next franc go to improve the system as a whole?
about_page.challenge_q2: How do allocations line up with national goals and PSTA 5?
about_page.challenge_q3: Which mix of investment reduces vulnerability to shocks?
about_page.provides_fsfsi: FSFI computes the Food System Financing Stress Index (FSFSI). The index combines 37 indicators in 8 components to measure financing stress across the food system. Budget and investment decisions can then rest on data rather than assumption.
about_page.card_assess_body: Shows how Rwanda's food system is performing on the dimensions that matter for outcomes and resilience.
about_page.card_gaps_body: Compares current results with benchmarks so that underperforming areas stand out.
about_page.card_invest_body: Shows where additional funding will do the most for national goals.
about_page.card_track_body: Links spending and results to PSTA 5 targets and year-on-year trends.
about_page.components_intro: For Rwanda, FSFI tracks 37 indicators in 8 components. They reflect the country's context and national priorities. Improving them through better allocation makes the food system more resilient and less likely to fail under shock.
about_page.gov_title: How government and partners use FSFI
about_page.gov_budget_body: MINAGRI, MINECOFIN and partners use the FSFSI and related tools to identify priority areas and justify allocation choices with evidence.
about_page.gov_perf_body: Check whether investments deliver the intended results and compare them with PSTA 5 targets.
about_page.gov_adv_body: Share quantitative evidence with development partners so that external finance supports national food system goals.
about_page.partners_intro: FSFI was developed with African and international research institutions.
about_page.cta_body: Sign in with your government credentials.

diagnosis.coverage_hint: Percentage = share of the performance gap absorbed by current financing (1 − stress/gap).
diagnosis.cumulative_level_hint: Classification of the cumulative (memory-adjusted) stress, when it differs from this year's.
diagnosis.table_footnote: Priority = stress class on component-level calibrated cut-points. 'Why' separates a gap that is not being financed from a gap that is heavily financed but has not yet closed; the percentage is the share of the gap absorbed by financing.
diagnosis.card_subtitle: Every stressed indicator in {{fy}} is sorted by why it is stressed: because the gap is not financed, or because it is financed but the outcome has not moved.
diagnosis.headline: {{money_n}} indicators carry {{money_stress}} of the national stress but receive {{money_budget}} of the budget (unfunded gaps). {{results_n}} indicators receive {{results_budget}} of the budget and produce {{results_stress}} of the stress (funded gaps, outcome lag).
diagnosis.imputed_hint: Placeholder benchmark: no reference data was found for this indicator, so its observed and benchmark values (and therefore the gap) are assumptions from the parameters sheet, not measurements. The financing side (budget, coverage) is real.
diagnosis.imputed_footnote: {{n}} of {{total}} indicators rest on placeholder benchmarks. For those, the 'results' side of the diagnosis is an assumption; the 'money' side is measured.

explainer.title: How to read the stress index
explainer.subtitle: What the number measures, how the four levels are set, and what "why" means.
explainer.what_p1: Every indicator has a benchmark. Its financing stress is the distance to that benchmark, reduced by how much financing it currently receives. A gap that is well financed produces little stress; the same gap with almost no financing produces stress close to the gap itself. Stress is therefore not "how bad the outcome is" but "how much of the shortfall is left unfinanced".
explainer.what_p2: Each component is the average of its indicators, and the national index is the weighted average of the components. 0 means every indicator is at its benchmark or fully financed towards it; 1 means a total shortfall with no financing behind it.
explainer.levels_title: How the four levels are set
explainer.levels_p1: The cut-points are not chosen by hand. They are the natural breaks (Fisher–Jenks) in Rwanda's own record: every indicator, component and national score saved for FY{{years}}, {{n}} component observations. Natural breaks place each boundary where the data itself splits into clusters, so a level groups scores that are genuinely alike and separates those that are not.
explainer.levels_p2: The cut-points are frozen until a calibration is run again. A change of level therefore always reflects a change in the data, never a change in the rule. Indicators are classified on their own scale because a single line is naturally more volatile than a component average.
explainer.levels_uncalibrated: The cut-points shown are engine defaults, not derived from Rwanda's data. Run the threshold calibration to replace them with natural breaks from the saved record.
explainer.meaning_low: Financing is broadly keeping pace with the benchmark gap. Monitor only.
explainer.meaning_medium: A meaningful shortfall that financing offsets only in part. Watch the trend; act if it persists.
explainer.meaning_high: A large shortfall with little financing behind it. This is the band Rwanda's stressed years fall into; it calls for reallocation.
explainer.meaning_critical: Among the most stressed observations on record. The gap is essentially unfinanced and should be a first-order budget priority.
explainer.fit_note: Fit of the grouping (goodness-of-variance fit, 1.0 = perfect separation): component level {{comp_gvf}} on {{comp_n}} observations; indicator level {{ind_gvf}} on {{ind_n}} observations.
explainer.system_inherits: The national score uses the component scale: the national index is a weighted mean of component scores, and fewer than {{min}} national observations exist so far (one per saved run and year). It gets its own breaks once there are at least {{min}}.
explainer.headline_p1: The large headline figure is cumulative stress: this year's result plus pressure carried over from earlier years, which fades only slowly. The smaller figure is this fiscal year alone. The two can sit in different levels; the headline badge and the critical-components count use the cumulative level, because that is what the system is actually carrying.
explainer.why_p1: A stress level on its own cannot tell you whether the problem is money or results. Financing coverage is the share of the benchmark gap that current financing absorbs. It splits every stressed line into one of three situations, again using natural breaks in Rwanda's record:
explainer.diag_unfunded_gap: The shortfall is real and is not being financed. More or better-targeted budget is the lever.
explainer.diag_partially_funded_gap: Financing is present but covers only part of the gap. Both the budget line and its delivery deserve attention.
explainer.diag_funded_gap: Financing is largely in place but the outcome has not yet responded. Look at delivery, lag and absorption rather than at the budget.
explainer.diag_at_benchmark: No material gap to the benchmark. Maintain.
explainer.coverage_note: Coverage cut-points are natural breaks on {{n}} indicator observations with a material gap, FY{{years}}.

assessment_page.page_subtitle: Run and review the FSFSI by fiscal year. Engine outputs are saved for audit and comparison.
assessment_page.saved_list_intro: Open a run to see component and indicator detail. Select up to four runs to compare headline figures.
assessment_page.compare_need_two: Select at least two runs to compare.
assessment_page.fsfsi_kpi_explainer: The headline uses the latest saved assessment for {{fy}}. When two figures appear, the headline is cumulative stress (pressure carried over from earlier years where the model applies it) and the smaller figure is this fiscal year alone. A saved run in the list shows its own point-in-time FSFSI. It matches the dashboard only when it is the same save, weighting and scenario as the run behind the summary.
assessment_page.efficiency_hint: Optimal FSFSI divided by actual FSFSI for this assessment. A value of 1.0 means actual stress equals the modelled optimal mix. Lower values mean stress is higher than the optimal benchmark, which indicates room to improve allocation.
assessment_page.detail_vs_dashboard_note: The KPI card at the top shows cumulative FSFSI when the backend provides it. This panel shows the point-in-time FSFSI for this save. If the figures differ, compare cumulative with point-in-time and check the weighting and scenario below.
assessment_page.gap_legend: Performance gap: a tick means the indicator is on or above its benchmark (gap near 0). An arrow with a value shows the distance from the benchmark. It is not a trend over time.
assessment_page.indicators_subtitle: Observed vs benchmark, stress and why for each indicator in "{{run}}". Click a group above or use the Why filter to narrow the table.
assessment_page.gap_tooltip_off_benchmark: Gap from benchmark for this indicator. The arrow shows size, not a year-on-year trend.
assessment_page.breakdown_subtitle: Financing stress and budget share by component. Colours follow the engine's priority levels.
assessment_page.breakdown_vs_budget_note: These figures differ from 'Data confidence' in Budget Analysis, which measures mapping traceability (direct versus fallback lines). They use the same mapped budgets as model inputs and report FSFSI stress, gaps against benchmarks and, below, where reallocation toward the optimal mix would reduce stress most.
assessment_page.priorities_subtitle: Ranked by financing stress (unique indicators). Budget lines refer to the modelled optimal mix.

optimization_page.title: Budget optimization
optimization_page.subtitle: Allocation analysis from the FSFI engine. It compares your mapped sector budgets with an optimal mix that minimises FSFSI for the same total envelope.
optimization_page.method_note: Uses the latest saved assessment for the selected fiscal year, with the same weighting and scenario. Results are indicative rebalancing signals, not appropriation instructions.
optimization_page.fy_selector_hint: Selects the assessment that provides the inputs. Only fiscal years with a saved assessment are listed.
optimization_page.no_assessment_title: No assessment for this fiscal year
optimization_page.no_assessment_body: Run an FSFSI assessment first. Optimization then loads automatically for the latest save in that year.
optimization_page.preview_title: What you will see when the engine has run
optimization_page.preview_running_body: The engine is computing efficiency, reallocation and return on investment from your latest saved assessment. This usually takes a few seconds, and up to a minute under load.
optimization_page.preview_idle_body: Preview of inputs and outputs. Results refresh when you change the fiscal year or re-run.
optimization_page.preview_output_efficiency: Efficiency index, current versus optimal FSFSI, and component-level gaps
optimization_page.preview_output_reallocation: Prioritised reallocation moves within the same total budget
optimization_page.preview_output_roi: Ranking of components by stress reduction per billion RWF
optimization_page.time_hint: Typical runtime: a few seconds to about one minute for all three panels.
optimization_page.results_lead: For this assessment, point-in-time FSFSI of {{current}} could fall to about {{optimal}} with an optimal mix. Modelled financing slack against that benchmark is about {{waste}}%.
optimization_page.rerun_title: Runs the same three optimization steps again for the current assessment
optimization_page.card_efficiency_sub: Current mapped allocations compared with the model's optimal shares for the same total budget. Shows where stress reduction is being left unused.
optimization_page.card_reallocation_sub: Prioritised shifts between components while keeping the total envelope from the assessment.
optimization_page.card_roi_sub: Ranks components by modelled stress reduction per billion RWF reallocated.

investment.title: Investment strategy
investment.subtitle: See how your programme's financing could lower Rwanda's food system financing stress (FSFSI) beyond what the national strategic plan already projects. Choose a plan, enter your programme and spending by year, then run the model. The result shows how far additional investment moves stress below the plan's path and toward its milestones.
investment.baseline_year_hint: The plan's baseline fiscal year is the assessment anchor, shown under your plan selection. Indicator budgets come from that assessment. Implementation amounts are entered for each horizon year below.
investment.baseline_year_hint_short: Budgets come from the plan's baseline assessment. The multi-year plan supplies projected FSFSI for the comparison years.
investment.persona_help: Changes how results are labelled. The model is the same; the interpretation differs for internal planning and external financing.
investment.results_framing_ministry: Use this run to show how further mapped spending could deepen the stress reductions already built into the national plan. See the note above.
investment.results_framing_donor: Use this run to show how your financing adds to the national plan. It builds on the same trajectory and can help the country beat its projected stress. See the note above.
investment.results_framing_partner: Use this run to show partners how additional support complements PSTA 5 and the plan's FSFSI path, and where it could take outcomes beyond the baseline projection.
investment.alignment_score_explainer: The PSTA 5 engine scores alignment from 0 to 100. A score of 100 means your envelope's shares across priority areas match national targets on average. Lower scores mean larger gaps.
investment.alignment_scale_note: Each percentage point of average deviation from priority area targets costs about 2 points on this scale. See the methodology in Strategic Planning.
investment.psta_gap_alert_title: Large gap from the national priority mix
investment.psta_gap_alert_item: {{code}}: your envelope allocates {{actual}}% against a national target of {{target}}% (shortfall {{gap}} pp).
investment.psta_gap_footer: Expect questions if a priority area with a high national target receives none of the modelled envelope through the indicators you selected.
investment.indicator_moves_caption: Stress (υ) and weighted stress (ωυ). Positive deltas mean stress fell for that indicator in this counterfactual.
investment.delta_stress_hint: Change in raw indicator financing stress before weighting.
investment.delta_weighted_hint: Change in weighted contribution to system stress.
investment.no_plans_for_year: No saved plans for this baseline year. Create one under Strategic Planning.
investment.no_plans_any: No saved strategic plans. Create one under Strategic Planning.
investment.plan_baseline_line: Plan baseline FY{{fy}}. Trajectory baseline FSFSI {{fsfsi}} (from the saved plan summary).
investment.schedule_help: Enter spending for each fiscal year in the plan horizon. At least one year must be greater than 0. The engine treats the total across years as one envelope, split evenly across the selected indicators.
investment.need_schedule_amount: Enter a positive amount in at least one implementation year.
investment.no_plan: Select a strategic plan linked to an assessment.
investment.project_year_help: Must be a fiscal year within the plan's horizon. Targets and projected FSFSI come from that plan year.
investment.no_horizon: Select a plan with yearly plans loaded
investment.need_project_year: Choose the fiscal year in which the project would run.
investment.vs_strategic_plan: What your investment adds to the national plan
investment.additionality_panel_subtitle: Financing stress (FSFSI) for FY{{fy}}. Lower means less pressure.
investment.step_assessment_hint: Saved budgets, before your extra envelope
investment.step_plan_trajectory_hint: National plan path for this year, before your add-on
investment.step_with_envelope_hint: Same baseline plus your mapped financing
investment.step_flow_caption: Each step shows how stress falls further when your financing is added to Rwanda's plan.
investment.additional_reduction_vs_trajectory: Extra stress reduction against the plan trajectory
investment.additional_reduction_vs_trajectory_hint: Plan projection minus with-envelope FSFSI: your contribution beyond the plan's projected path.
investment.additional_reduction_vs_milestone_hint: Milestone minus with-envelope FSFSI. Positive means lower stress than the milestone in this run.
investment.additionality_worse_than_plan: In this run the envelope FSFSI is above the plan projection. Check the weighting, scenario or indicator mix.
investment.delta_vs_plan_projected: Gap against the plan trajectory (negative means lower stress than projected)
investment.delta_vs_plan_target: Gap against the milestone (negative means lower stress than the milestone)
investment.additionality_lead: For FY{{fy}}, the saved national plan projects an FSFSI of {{plan_proj}}. Your mapped envelope ({{total_bn}} bn RWF in this run) brings the modelled FSFSI to {{with_env}}.
investment.additionality_extra: That is {{vs_traj}} index points of additional stress reduction against the plan trajectory, and {{vs_mil}} against the plan milestone. In this exercise your financing adds to the plan and speeds progress down the stress scale.
investment.no_assessment_year: No assessment for this fiscal year
investment.split_note: The total is split evenly across the selected indicators as additional mapped financing, in the same units as national budget lines.
investment.need_indicators: Select at least one indicator that your programme targets.
investment.need_total: Enter a positive total investment in billions of RWF.
investment.filter_placeholder: Search by code, name or component…
investment.no_indicators: This assessment has no indicator rows. Run an assessment for this year first.
investment.per_indicator_bn_note: {{amt}} bn RWF applied to each selected indicator (equal split).
investment.results_placeholder: Complete the form and run the engine to see baseline FSFSI, with-project FSFSI and the stress reduction (Δ FSFSI).
investment.baseline_vs_plan_explainer: Baseline FSFSI uses the budgets from the plan's assessment year. The stepped panel shows the plan's trajectory for FY{{fy}}, then your envelope. Additionality is how much further stress falls beyond that trajectory. It is not a comparison against the government's own plan.
investment.delta_fsfsi_note: Positive values mean lower modelled financing stress for the same indicator performance. This is a counterfactual budget exercise, not a forecast of development outcomes.
investment.psta_envelope_note: Uses only your additional amounts. Shows how your allocation compares with national priority area targets.
investment.no_indicator_touch: No indicator received additional financing in this run.

planning.title: Strategic Planning
planning.subtitle: Multi-year FSFSI trajectory and MTEF for national decision making.
planning.no_assessment_message: Run an FSFI assessment for the selected fiscal year to enable strategic planning and the MTEF.
planning.parameters_help: Set the target and horizon. Both the multi-year plan and the 3-year MTEF are generated. The budget growth rate applies to both.
planning.horizon_start_fy_hint: Maps horizon rows to fiscal year labels (Year 2 is this year plus one, and so on). Defaults to the year after the assessment year.
planning.alignment_help: Expand a year and enter component budgets in billions of RWF. The national total is the sum of those lines, and the percentage split updates as you type. The tool compares your total with the plan and projects cumulative FSFSI for your mix, using the same stress rules as strategic planning.
planning.alignment_cumulative_note: Enter the budget you propose for each component below. The tool compares your allocation with the optimal plan and projects the national financing stress score for that mix and total.
planning.alignment_mix_help: Amounts add up to your national total. 'Your %' is derived from your split and always sums to 100%.
planning.alignment_fsfsi_compare: Cumulative FSFSI after your allocation (this horizon year)
planning.alignment_worse: Higher cumulative stress than the optimal plan for this year. Review your mix and total.
planning.alignment_above_target: Above the planned milestone target for this year.
planning.alignment_prior_missing: Prior-year plan data is missing, so years 2 onward cannot be simulated.
planning.alignment_sim_failed: Could not run the allocation simulation.
planning.alignment_actual_hint: This year's actual allocation is recorded
planning.alignment_save_failed: Could not save the actual allocation.
planning.alignment_footnote: The simulation uses the planning weights and scenario selected above. It does not re-run a full indicator-level assessment. For official scores, run an assessment once budgets are fixed.
planning.regenerate_plans_hint: Runs the planner again with the current parameters and assessment. Use after changing targets, growth, weighting or scenario.
planning.workflow_hint: When results appear, use the tabs below the KPI cards to move between trajectory, components, budget alignment, MTEF and outcomes.
planning.tab_mtef_unavailable: MTEF results are not loaded. Generate plans from the same assessment, or open a saved plan that matches this run.
planning.save_state_note: Saving stores the parameters and the engine's strategic plan (trajectory and optimal mix). 'Save as actual' in Budget alignment is separate: it records the allocations you typed for tracking, and only works once a plan is saved.
planning.mtef_year3_off_track_title: Year 3 is off the MTEF path
planning.mtef_year3_off_track_intro: Projected FSFSI is {{projected}}, above the Year 3 policy corridor ({{policy}}) and/or the operational pacing target ({{operational}}). Lower is better on this index, so the 3-year envelope requires faster stress reduction than the current budget trajectory delivers.
planning.mtef_year3_off_track_levers: Options: raise annual budget growth in the parameters, revisit the MTEF improvement percentage, choose a pacing curve that matches fiscal capacity, or shift more of the envelope to the highest-stress components before raising the total.
planning.mtef_targets_curve_note: Policy targets follow the linear 3-year fiscal commitment line. Operational targets use the pacing curve you selected ({{curve}}).
planning.fiscal_mtef_row_yoy: Modelled change within the MTEF window: Year 1 to Year 2 {{y1y2}}%; Year 1 to Year 3 {{y1y3}}%.
planning.component_table_subtitle: Projected cumulative stress by component over the planning horizon. Recovery speed depends on each sector's dynamics and its share of the envelope.
planning.component_table_sort_hint: Rows are sorted by the largest reduction in cumulative stress first, not alphabetically or by budget size.
planning.component_policy_alert_lead: {{names}}: cumulative stress is still projected to rise for these components under the recommended mix.
planning.component_policy_alert_close: Consider moving funds from stable areas toward the sectors under the most persistent stress, while keeping the national total realistic.
planning.budget_increase_over_plan: Planned budget increase (by end of plan)
planning.budget_increase_hint: Extra budget over the plan needed to reach the target. This is not a funding gap.
planning.section_multiyear_desc: Trajectory, budget evolution and outcomes for the chosen planning horizon.
planning.section_mtef_desc: A separate rolling 3-year plan with its own improvement target and budget growth.
planning.trajectory_help: Projected FSFSI against the yearly target. The green line is the final target.
planning.insights_title: Expected outcomes, risks and success factors
planning.mtef_help: Rolling 3-year plan with an improvement target and budget growth.
planning.mtef_diff_note: The MTEF is a separate 3-year plan. It uses the improvement percentage and budget growth rate above. Its Year 3 target is baseline × (1 − improvement %), not the absolute target in the trajectory chart. Projected FSFSI can beat that target when budget growth is high.
planning.saved_plans_help: Open a stored plan, set one as active for the National Overview, or start a new draft. Select up to three plans to compare trajectories.
planning.saved_plans_empty: No saved plans for this fiscal year yet. Generate a plan below, then use Save plan.
planning.viewing_saved: You are viewing a saved plan. Adjust the parameters and click Generate plans to explore alternatives, or Start new plan to clear the canvas.
planning.compare_help: Parameters and projected FSFSI paths side by side (multi-year trajectory only).
planning.saved_invalid_json: This saved plan could not be loaded (missing data).
planning.saved_open_failed: Could not open the saved plan.
planning.compare_failed: Could not load plans for comparison.
planning.activate_failed: Could not set the active plan.
planning.saved_different_assessment: This plan was saved from a different assessment run than the one loaded now. Regenerate the assessment if you need figures aligned with current data.
planning.save_new_title: Save this plan as the official strategic plan
planning.save_new_help: Plan names must be unique within a fiscal year. Saving a new plan deactivates the previous active plan for that year.
planning.save_update_help: Changes to parameters or weighting regenerate the stored trajectory. A new name must also be unique for this fiscal year.
planning.delete_confirm: Delete this saved plan permanently? This cannot be undone.

budget_page.title: Budget Analysis
budget_page.subtitle: How Rwanda's agriculture and food system budget is mapped across components and fiscal years, in weighted LCU billions.
budget_page.scope_note: All series come from mapped budget data, not from FSFSI assessment scores.
budget_page.no_data: No mapped budget data yet. Run import_budget_mapping (pipeline step 1) first.
budget_page.metric_vol_hint: Standard deviation of year-on-year % change in the national weighted total
budget_page.metric_hhi_hint: Across components. Higher means more concentrated.
budget_page.metric_mapping_confidence_hint: Mapped lines as a share of all lines in FY{{year}} (100% minus fallback). Higher means stronger traceability to programmes.
budget_page.chart_national_help: Sum of weighted indicator allocations in billions LCU.
budget_page.chart_spike_note: +{{yoy}}% from FY{{prevYear}} to FY{{year}}. Sharp jumps can reflect real spending growth, programme reclassification or changes in mapping method. Validate before reading them as a policy outcome.
budget_page.chart_general_caveat: Totals combine directly mapped and fallback allocations. Read this series together with data confidence and the mapping quality table.
budget_page.chart_share_title: Largest components, share of national total
budget_page.chart_share_help: Percent of the national weighted budget by component (top five in the latest year).
budget_page.insights_subtitle: Decision-oriented readouts from the composition model. Use the reference tables for audit detail.
budget_page.drift_help: Change in percentage points of the national weighted total.
budget_page.section_reference_intro: Detailed lines for ministry analysts and development partner review.
budget_page.movers_help: Ranks use weighted LCU for each year. Level Δ% and CAGR require a positive allocation in the first year (and, for CAGR, in the last year). Where the start is zero, growth is undefined and the cell shows a dash. Share Δ (ppt) is always defined: the change in this indicator's share of the national mapped total.
budget_page.mover_cagr_hint: Geometric growth of this indicator's weighted total, shown only when the first and last years are both greater than zero.
budget_page.mover_cagr_caveat: An extreme CAGR usually means the first-year allocation was very small. The figure is correct but misleading as a headline. Use share change (ppt) and level context instead.
budget_page.mover_footnote_cagr: * Extreme CAGR or near-zero starting allocation. Hover over the cell for detail.
budget_page.mover_level_hint: Percent change in this indicator's weighted total against the first year, shown only when the first year is greater than zero.
budget_page.mover_share_hint: Change in percentage points of the national mapped total (first year versus last year).
budget_page.quality_help: Mapped budget lines compared with fallback estimates. More fallback means weaker links to programmes.
budget_page.snapshot_help: Indicator table for the last year of the window, using the same definitions as the pipeline.
budget_page.snapshot_auto_hint: The year-end composition loads automatically for the end of the current window.
